status: PROPOSAL, NOT LOCKED. The three agreed test versions (v0.61.0 size, v0.62.0 noise, v0.63.0 noise and size) are done, so the direction choice is James's. agreed_direction: James, Nov 2 2026 20:10 EST: after v0.60.0 spend 2-3 versions testing how far the new method goes at larger sizes and with noise, prefer good ideas over budget bumps, then choose deliberately between a black-box certification tool and a messier real-world problem.

choice_for_james.A_tool: Package certify/32s as a black-box certification tool: a library entry point and CLI that takes any system exposing reset/act/read, declared N <= 24, read_bits 2, eps_bar, delta, and returns ID/IDF/UNDECIDED with the exact certified envelope printed beside it; plus a conformance suite (the 045-066 worlds as fixtures) and a short operator guide. Low research risk; the product value depends on how often real systems fit the envelope, which is unknown (Open).
choice_for_james.B_real_world: Aim Brute at a messier real-world problem: hidden state of real software or a real device through its public I/O, where noise is not iid, re-reads may disturb the state and the true size is not known. High value if it works; the current guarantee does not cover those conditions (Exact), so new ideas are needed (for example a size-free stopping argument or a correlated-noise model), not bigger budgets.
choice_for_james.C_bridge_recommended: First do one small version that serves both: certify the hidden control state of UNMODIFIED real software through its public I/O, inside the current envelope. If James then picks A, the adapter is the tool's first real input; if he picks B, the targets grow from here. Recommended because it tests real-system fit cheaply and pre-empts neither choice (Inferred).
choice_for_james.credit: The bridge idea was drafted by executor-A (/tmp/s67/PLAN_067_DRAFT.md, about 10:37 EST) and adopted here by executor-B.

targets.T1: Python stdlib incremental UTF-8 decoder (codecs.getincrementaldecoder('utf-8')('replace')). Actions are byte classes {0x41 ASCII, 0x80 continuation, 0xE1 3-byte lead}; the 2-bit reading is (emitted any char, emitted U+FFFD). Probe (Observed, /tmp/s67/utf8probe.py, suffixes up to length 4): 3 distinct states.
targets.T2: Same decoder with 0xF1 (4-byte lead) in place of 0xE1: 4 distinct states (Observed, same probe).
targets.T3_open: A larger real target (html.parser.HTMLParser tokenizer states, or a small real protocol state machine) still to be found and measured; required so the bridge is not only tiny worlds (Open).

bridge_design_sketch.adapter: a new non-core module (scripts/ or adapters/, not brute/) that wraps the target as reset/act/read; brute/ stays host-agnostic
bridge_design_sketch.ground_truth: white-box, from the target's source and an independent exhaustive probe, used only by the recount, never by the identifier
bridge_design_sketch.arms: noise-free certify/32p and certify/32s with iid bit flips at eps 0.30 injected by the adapter, per target; plus one arm with a deliberately disturbing re-read (a read that also feeds a byte) reported as out-of-envelope, never gated
bridge_design_sketch.gates_to_lock_later: sound vs white-box truth; equality of noisy and noise-free records; 0 settled-bit errors; reads <= 0.35x the fixed rule; reference audit; exact recount; KILL-bounded runner as in 066
bridge_design_sketch.honest_framing: T1 and T2 are tiny (3 and 4 states), so the bridge tests the real-system path and its I/O fit, not scale. The noise is still injected iid, so it is not yet the messier problem itself.

what_this_does_not_decide: which branch Brute takes after the bridge; whether the bridge runs at all if James prefers A or B directly
next_step: James picks A, B, or C (the bridge). Then a locked plan file with seed-free target list, frozen gates and a ledgered build_authorization_067.
